criteria.argument_values: Negative, non-integer, or overflowing max_rows fails before launch as unsupported_value with path max_rows, while row_limit fires only when the bounded fetch observes more rows than max_rows. Argument defects and observed overflow stay distinct errors.
criteria.limit_unified: Every max_rows problem, whether a defective argument or an over-full result, reports row_limit with the supplied limit. One error covers the whole bound regardless of when the defect is detected.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot separate these error assignments, or neither keeps the required contracts.

max_rows_errors.instructions: Choose which error reports defective max_rows arguments versus observed row overflow. Use common and topics.max_rows_errors.

criteria.connect_await: pool_open constructs the client, awaits the native connect operation, and only then returns the pool. Refusals and authentication failures surface as connection_failed during open, so an open pool has proven its connection.
criteria.lazy_documented: pool_open returns after construction without contacting the server. Connection state is revealed by the first query, and the documented contract states that open does not prove reachability.
criteria.probe_query: pool_open proves the connection by executing a fixed SELECT 1 round trip and discarding its row. Open performs real query work solely to test reachability.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot decide the establishment proof, or no candidate keeps the required contracts.

pool_open_proof.instructions: Choose what proves pool_open connected rather than merely constructing a lazy client. Use common and topics.pool_open_proof.

criteria.propagate_fault: Only PostgresError values classify into the query errors. Any other throw from the driver propagates to the generic fault path, so driver bugs stay visible as faults instead of masquerading as query outcomes.
criteria.query_failed_unknown: Every throw from the native tag call maps into the finite query errors. Shapes without a SQLSTATE or driver code report query_failed with code unknown, so no native failure escapes classification.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot decide unknown-shape handling, or neither rule keeps the required contracts.

unknown_failures.instructions: Choose how native failures outside the known PostgresError shapes classify. Use common and topics.unknown_failures.

fixed_constraints: The catalogue binds pool_open to the credentials_missing and connection_failed errors, and binds each query operation to its fixed subset of unsupported_value, connection_failed, query_failed, constraint_failed, row_missing, row_count, row_limit, and schema_mismatch. Native failures must map into these errors with sanitized fields; messages, details, URLs, and credentials never surface.

Measured Bun 1.4.2 behavior: constructing SQL never contacts the server, even with an unreachable port. Awaiting connect resolves to the identical client instance, repeats idempotently, and throws ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_REFUSED or the server error on failure. Queries after close throw ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_CLOSED. Server errors carry the 5-character SQLSTATE in errno plus the constraint name when one applies; message and detail text can embed row values.

I35 binds the top-level LIMIT as a value: 2 for one/optional shapes and max_rows+1 for many shapes. max_rows arrives as a caller-supplied integer; a defective argument is detectable before launch while observed overflow is detectable only after the bounded fetch. Bad parameters must never launch a query.

Checked descriptors hold parser-verified single statements, so a syntax failure from a bound descriptor implies a driver defect rather than author error. The runtime keeps a generic fault path that converts unexpected throws into standard failures.
common.purpose: Advise the Can implementation strictly from the evidence supplied here. Do not browse, implement, or explain. When candidates cannot be separated on the evidence, choose the marked uncertainty outcome.

max_rows_errors.facts: The catalogue offers both unsupported_value with a path and row_limit with a limit to query_rows. A negative max_rows or a max_rows whose successor escapes the 64-bit range is known before any native call; an over-full result is known only after. Both must refuse to silently widen or truncate the bound.

pool_open_proof.facts: Because construction is lazy, an open call that only constructs cannot distinguish a live database from a dead port, yet the catalogue still assigns connection_failed to pool_open. Awaiting connect performs the handshake without query work; a probe query performs the handshake plus a round trip whose row is discarded.

unknown_failures.facts: Every observed driver failure is a PostgresError with a code, and server failures add errno and often constraint. Non-PostgresError throws have not been observed; they could only arise from defects inside the driver or its bindings. Classification must stay finite either way.
